criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale - Include the following required information: • What is the spacecraft's primary mission? • Why is the mission needed? • How many spacecraft are used and why? • Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All four required items addressed with specific rationale and context for GBR. Single-satellite justification provided. Users identified as CSIRO/BOM with operator as university/government. References cited.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear engineering report structure with executive summary, TOC, headings, figures with captions, STK images. Grammar mostly sound. References in-text match bibliography but includes Wikipedia which violates guidance, and figure numbering inconsistent - prevents higher mark.

evidence.quote: This report outlines the intended designs and procedures involved in the construction
STK 3D view of orbit: 12 hours apart

technical_issues.issue: Uses Argument of Latitude u instead of argument of perigee/true anomaly for circular orbit without explanation of alternative; RAAN 27.33 described as launch facility location is incorrect conceptually.
Equatorial benefit overstated for SSO (retrograde polar launch loses equatorial rotation benefit); no delta-V or piggyback mass budget.
Access report shows duplicate entries and timing inconsistencies (Feb 3 09:28 listed after header) likely STK export error; not discussed.

overall: Strong, coherent SSO Earth observation mission for GBR with fluid lensing payload, well supported by STK simulations and trade studies. Meets all core requirements with only minor technical imprecisions and presentation lapses.

feedback.summary: You delivered a strong, coherent GBR Earth-observation mission with fluid lensing. You met all core requirements with STK evidence. To strengthen, correct key orbital terminology and SSO launch physics, clean STK outputs, and tighten referencing and figure numbering for a fully professional finish.
next_steps: In Mission Design - Orbit, replace Argument of Latitude u with ω and ν for circular orbits, and define RAAN correctly - it is not launch site latitude. Add a brief note if you use u as alternative.

In Mission Design - Launch, qualify the equatorial benefit for your retrograde SSO - explain why Guiana is still chosen despite rotation penalty, and add a simple delta-V and mass/margin budget for Vega E vs Vega C fallback.

In Ground Control & Communications and Bibliography, remove duplicate/timing errors in your access report (Image 1) with a 1-sentence quality check, fix figure numbering, and replace Wikipedia with primary sources per guidance.

criteria.C1: You addressed all 4 items well: coral reef monitoring purpose, acidity/bleaching rationale, single-sat justification for simplicity, and CSIRO/BOM users with university operator. For top of Accomplished, deepen literature support for user needs and payload requirement.
criteria.C2: Excellent work covering Vega E from Guiana with trade study, SSO table with a=6971km and i=97.79° vs altitude plot, STK screenshots, and 5 passes/day ~580s plus 5-yr life and drag sail EOL. Next level needs corrected u definition, RAAN concept, SSO launch physics, and delta-V/mass budget.
criteria.C3: Your Conclusion effectively synthesises evidence: Vega E selection with Vega C risk, polar SSO for illumination, comms frequency and EOL. To reach higher Accomplished, quantify key residual impacts for Australia and final requirements closure.
criteria.C4: Clear report structure with Executive Summary, TOC, headed sections, and captioned STK figures. For higher Accomplished, make figure numbering sequential, ensure all references are authoritative per guidance, and proof Table 1 consistency.
